description.narrative: Oxfam works with communities before, during and after crises to build their resilience to shocks, save lives, and together address the root causes of crises, including the underlying causes of poverty and the factors that can drive individuals below the poverty line and into crisis. Anticipatory action can be one of the ways to build resilience to shocks, but it has primarily been implementedin the context of extreme weather events. In anticipatory action models, socio-economic vulnerability is usually approached as a static condition, for example as part of targeting processes, but it does not consider the fluctuations in socio-economic vulnerability as a result of economic shocks. Through this project, Oxfam and RECA will develop a practical multi-hazard decision-making model for anticipatory action that includes the risk of economic shocks as one of the main drivers of humanitarian need to enable vulnerable groups to mitigate the impact of shocks on their lives and livelihoods. Embedding economic shocks in a multi-hazard model requiresinvestment since the methodology isn't readily available to understand and forecast economic shocks, and will need to be developed through this project. However, this can build on available economic and vulnerability indicators that are already used in humanitarian programming, especially in protracted crisis contexts, and that are used in social protection programming. The multi-hazard modelwill build on existing work in anticipatory action and social protection, and it will combine economic vulnerability with other (contextual) drivers of humanitarian need. It may therefore include indicators for both climate-induced and human-made hazards.The proposed model for multi-hazard anticipatory action will consider that economic shocks and economic vulnerability can manifest in different ways, but also how economic vulnerability can be a driver of humanitarian need. In this context, (household) economic vulnerability refers to the coping capacity of a household to withstand shocks, including unexpected or increased expenses or income fluctuations. This project will have two main results, with the first result focusing on the development of the multi-hazard anticipatory action model, and the second result focuses on documentation of the process of developing the model for sector-wide influencing. While the project will focus on the Nigerien context, the process of the development of the multi-hazard AA model will be used to demonstrate the relevance of economic shocks in anticipatory action and influence stakeholders in the sector to take a similar approach. Theproject focuses on the process of developing a multi-hazard anticipatory action model and it does not include the implementation ofactivities based on activation of the model.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education for all, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam Novibs main office is based in The Netherlands, it supports the work of a network of local offices, the implementation of global projects, fund raising, campaigning and advocacy. The Hub Niamey Niger exists since 2006 as a humanitarian field office and since 2012 as the decentralized Country office for Oxfam Novib, dealing with all the development and humanitarian themes like Sustainable livelihoods, Right to Basic services, Humanitarian and resilience interventions, The right to be heard and the right to an Identity, including women's rights and sexual and reproductive health rights. The Country Office in Niger works with local partners to realize the vision of a Niger without poverty
